name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
sub_region: Kaski District, Gandaki Province (Annapurna Conservation Area, Modi Khola valley)

difficulty.notes: Non-technical; many stone staircases (notably Chhomrong-Bamboo). Max sleeping altitude 4,130 m. Daily walking 5-7 h. [s4][s6]

duration_days.basis: full trip Kathmandu-Kathmandu (7 trekking days from Pokhara)
duration_days.notes: Standard is ~7 trekking days from Pokhara without Poon Hill, ~9 with Poon Hill; 5 days possible only with a jeep to Jhinu and no reserve. Kathmandu packages run 10-15 days. Approaches: via Ghandruk (south), via Ghorepani/Poon Hill (west), or jeep to Jhinu (shortest). [s6]

itinerary.route: Kathmandu - Pokhara (drive 6-7 h or flight ~25 min)

itinerary.notes: Large Gurung village; altitude listed 1,940-2,010 m. [s4][s5]
Last large settlement before the Sanctuary. [s4]
A short day into the Annapurna Sanctuary that eases the climb to Base Camp. The route crosses avalanche paths below MBC. [s4][s7]

itinerary.route: Machhapuchhre Base Camp - Annapurna Base Camp
itinerary.notes: Sunset on Annapurna I and the walls of the Sanctuary.

itinerary.route: Jhinu Danda - Siwai/Nayapul - drive to Pokhara
Pokhara - Kathmandu; departure or extra night

best_seasons.notes: Rhododendron bloom above ~2,800 m in March-April. [s4] Winter snowfall increases avalanche hazard on the Deurali-MBC section. [s7]

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP)
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per foreign national (SAARC NPR 1,000), tax included; single entry; double if bought at checkpoint

guide_requirements: NTB lists the Poon Hill-ABC trek among routes where a licensed guide via a registered agency is mandatory since the revised TIMS provision effective 31 March 2023. [s3] 2026 reports describe staffed checkpoints at Birethanti, Ghandruk and Chhomrong checking ACAP and increasingly guide credentials. [s8]

logistics.notes: Teahouses at every overnight stop; Chhomrong is the last large settlement with shops. [s4]

highlights: Annapurna Sanctuary amphitheatre with Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna and Machhapuchhre [s7]
Rhododendron and bamboo forest of the Modi Khola gorge [s4]
Jhinu Danda hot springs on the descent [s6]
risks: Avalanche paths between Deurali and Machhapuchhre Base Camp, especially after heavy snowfall [s7]
AMS from fast gain (Deurali to ABC ~900 m in a day) [s5]
Knee strain from long stone staircases [s4]

acclimatization.notes: Standard itinerary has no dedicated rest day; sleeping at MBC (3,700 m) instead of Deurali splits the gain. Acclimatisation flagged as tight by planning tools for Deurali-ABC. [s5][s6]

secondary_keywords: Annapurna Base Camp trek from Pokhara

unverified: Whether a TIMS card is actually required/checked on ABC in 2026 (NTB says yes; multiple operators say only ACAP is checked).
Minor altitude differences between sources (Ghandruk 1,940-2,010 m; Deurali 3,200-3,230 m).
